subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Hedonic Framing: Bundling Gains and Losses
description: Learn Hedonic Framing: Bundling Gains and Losses in one minute.

hook.text: Getting two $50 gifts on different days feels better than one $100 gift. Same total, more joy.

buildup.text: Thaler's hedonic framing rules: separate gains to maximize pleasure and combine losses to minimize pain.

discovery.text: Because the value function is concave for gains, two smaller gains produce more total happiness than one big one.

twist.text: For losses, the opposite: rip off the bandaid. One big loss is less painful than the same amount in small chunks.

climax.text: Good news? Spread it out. Bad news? Deliver it all at once. This is hedonic framing applied to life.

punchline.text: Spread the joy. Bundle the pain.

quiz.question: Why do two $50 gifts feel better than one $100 gift?
options: The value function is concave for gains, making two hits of pleasure exceed one
